definitions.explanation: Moisture that forms on surfaces at night.

examples.japanese: {草|くさ}に{露|つゆ}が{降|お}りている。
examples.english: Dew has formed on the grass.

examples.japanese: {露|つゆ}ほども{疑|うたが}わない。
examples.english: I don't doubt it in the slightest.

notes:
{露|つゆ} means dew—water droplets that form on surfaces overnight.

HOMOPHONE:
{露|つゆ} (dew) and {梅雨|つゆ} (rainy season) have the same pronunciation but different kanji and meanings.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {露|つゆ}が{降|お}りる: dew forms/falls
- {露|つゆ}に{濡|ぬ}れる: to get wet with dew

FIGURATIVE USE:
{露|つゆ}ほども〜ない means 'not even a tiny bit':
- {露|つゆ}ほども{知|し}らない: I don't know at all
- {露|つゆ}ほども{疑|うたが}わない: I don't doubt in the slightest

COMPOUNDS:
- {朝露|あさつゆ}: morning dew
- {露天|ろてん}: open-air, outdoor
- {露天|ろてん}{風呂|ぶろ}: outdoor bath

LITERARY NOTE:
Dew is a classic image in Japanese poetry ({和歌|わか}, {俳句|はいく}), symbolizing transience and the fleeting nature of life.
